summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found one obvious reference operator, Stride, and three adjacent public companies with plausible direct or second-order exposure to online education operations, workforce-aligned postsecondary pathways, employer education partnerships, education technology services, payments, and student-loan-adjacent infrastructure. The strongest direct K-12 virtual-school exposure is Stride. Grand Canyon Education and Strategic Education are more postsecondary/workforce-pathway exposed than K-12, while Nelnet is a second-order infrastructure hypothesis through education technology services, payments, systems, and loan-servicing infrastructure. No buy/sell view is implied. Layer 1B expansion focuses on the scarce operating and infrastructure layer behind virtual schooling and career-linked education: state/district-approved operating capacity, enrollment and student-support workflows, education payments/servicing systems, university-partner service platforms, employer-partner workforce pathways, simulation/VR learning tools, and compliance-heavy postsecondary bridge programs. The reference anchor is Stride because it directly serves K-12, career learning, professional skills training, and talent development across all 50 states and over 100 countries. Underfollowed discovery candidates are not generic edtech apps; they are service, systems, payments, employer-partner, and hybrid-program operators that could benefit if institutions outsource more of the operational burden of online, career, and licensure-oriented education.
